claims.statement: For the same fixed irrational phase alpha=(sqrt(5)-1)/2 throughout, p_k=(1+cos(2 pi alpha k))/2, arbitrary homogeneous n-state stochastic P, initial distribution mu and terminal readout f in [0,1]^n, with identical wait commands and one terminal read, N_alpha(T,epsilon)=Theta_(alpha,epsilon)(T^(1/3)) for each fixed 0<epsilon<1/4. The terminal readout receives only the evolved state and is not additionally handed k or an external lookup table. At zero error separately T<=N_alpha(T,0)<=T+1; an ideal qubit realizes the probabilities. This is not a runtime, physical clock, joint-output-process, or practical computing advantage. An ordinary counter/cosine uses O(log T) bits and phase/gate precision is O(log(T/epsilon)).

Preserve the expected subgroup-image bound under strict triangular layers and the stated shared-category/uniform-mask independence premise, plus the exact HNF/local callable prototype for cyclic Z/MZ. The implementation is cyclic only. N610 base-p digit inclusion is proved for prime-power moduli only; mixed-prime CRT needs joint categories and cross-component forcing, and generic finite-group access does not establish polynomial bit cost. In the matched root 3,000-draw Z/4 run, subgroup HNF used 5.760 fresh events and 3.195 s versus 7.013 events and 0.405 s for the digit incumbent. Fewer random events did not win on total measured time. No new output class or practical advantage is established.

At fixed deterministic cumulative fluence per attempted site and unconditioned occupied output, the blind writer has q*=p sigma_L/[p sigma_L+(1-p)sigma_H], while vacancy-history stopping is informative and outside that quantifier. In the ideal renewal, irradiate one fresh atom until ejection or screening fluence d; an ejection triggers independent fresh refill/restart, while a complete survivor is accepted and protected. Then q(d)=p exp(-sigma_H d)/[p exp(-sigma_H d)+(1-p)exp(-sigma_L d)]. At planning p=.01109 and central 95 kV cross sections sigma_L=56.6 mb and sigma_H=2.1 mb, the nominal 90% calculation gives EXPECTED costs of about 105 attempts, 104 refills and 1.959e13 target electrons/nm^2. Retry and dose tails are unbounded; finite caps reduce yield. These are conditional expectations at those inputs, not a general 90% cost. 0.298 J/nm^2 is incident kinetic energy per uniformly addressed area, not absorbed heat, per-site energy or wall-plug cost. Same-atom no-ejection record, independent fresh refill/composition, preserved repaired-site rates, neighbor protection, event/reset and final readout are unacquired.

Two passive systems can have identical accessible scattering and total-loss flags but exchange target/parasitic sink labels, so even adaptive external control cannot infer the hidden sink from that interface. A passive one-port resonator can reduce total loss while a new target sink absorbs positive energy. The positive finite-power saturable-bucket theorem is stated for 0<a<b and requires (ab)^(1/3)(a^(1/3)+b^(1/3))<=1, along with fixed delivered target-plane power, full complex control, complete energy collection, a qualified single-pass homogeneous saturable absorber, acquired response and reset. Nonlinear bucket and iTRAN methods are strong incumbents; no new demonstrated capability or practical advantage follows.

Dual-rail loss provides a known erasure sector, and the 2026 cavity SWS CZ is positive prior evidence. Loss during its coupler-target cross-Kerr can leave a correlated unknown partial phase even when a final erasure flag is known. The proposed coupler-inclusive monitor requires about an 8 ns event-time uncertainty for a stated small-angle phase-error budget whose infidelity contribution is quadratic in residual phase; the cited continuous-monitor experiment used a much longer integration window on a different transmon platform and does not demonstrate that timing for the SWS cavity path. Which-path dephasing, monitor-induced loss/backaction, full-circuit performance and matched cost remain open. Credit primary experimental authors; no new capability or quantum advantage is claimed.
